newsitem.title: HUNGARY: NEW ROMANIAN ENVOY TO VISIT HUNGARY THIS MONTH.
newsitem.headline: NEW ROMANIAN ENVOY TO VISIT HUNGARY THIS MONTH.

text.p: Hungary on Friday said new Romanian Foreign minister Adrian Severin will visit Hungary this month, probably on December 27.
"Mr Severin has accepted our invitation and will probably come on December 27, although we have yet to receive official confirmation," a foreign ministry source told Reuters.
"We expect the confirmation later today," he said.

The decision by Severin to come to Budapest so soon after taking office is expected to set the seal on the warming of relations between the countries since Romanian President Emil Constantinescu's election victory last month and his decision to include ethnic Hungarians in his government.
Hungary on Tuesday ratified a friendship treaty signed earlier this year by Constantinescu's predecessor Ion Iliescu and Hungarian Prime Minister Gyula Horn.

The basic treaty guarantees borders and enshrines political and cultural rights for Romania's 1.6 million-strong ethnic Hungarian population, an issue which had previously caused tension between the two countries.
The new Romanian governent led by Prime Minister Victor Ciorbea, was sworn in on Thursday.
